links.outcome: Deployed model sensitivity and specificity by sociodemographic subgroup after deployment
links.effect: Sensitivity 70.1% overall with no significant subgroup variation; specificity varied by age (<60: 93%, 60-80: 90%, >80: 84%, P<.001) but not other subgroups.
links.quote: Model specificity varied by age, <60 years: 93% (95% Confidence Interval [CI] 91-95%), 60-80 years: 90% (95%CI 87-92%), and >80 years: 84% (95%CI 79-88%), P < .001, but not other subgroups.

links.outcome: Care processes and patient outcomes across sociodemographic subgroups after deployment
links.effect: Implementation associated with increased code status documentation among patients experiencing homelessness, without significant differences in other care processes or outcomes.
links.quote: CHARTwatch implementation was associated with an increase in code status documentation among patients experiencing homelessness, without significant differences in other care processes or outcomes.

links.outcome: Subgroup performance gaps in model specificity and sensitivity
links.effect: No significant sensitivity variation across subgroups; specificity lower with older age (84% in >80 vs 93% in <60, P<.001); no other subgroup differences.
links.quote: Model sensitivity was 70.1% overall, with no significant variation across subgroups.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of a real-time clinical deployment of an early warning system (CHARTwatch) assessing downstream sociodemographic bias, care process disparities, and patient outcomes.
